messages.content: Write a blog post announcing version 2.0 of an API client library. Around 250 words.

# Fetchkit 2.0

Fetchkit 2.0 shipped this morning.

Version 1 got one thing wrong at the root. Every response was parsed as JSON before it reached you. That held up until somebody piped a 200 MB CSV through it and watched their Node process fall over. 2.0 gives you the raw stream and steps back.

Three smaller changes.

Retries are configured per request. Write `retry: { attempts: 4, on: [429, 503] }` on the single endpoint that misbehaves instead of turning it on everywhere and crossing your fingers; backoff respects `Retry-After`.

Errors now carry the response, and I think that is the change people will feel first. Read `err.response.status` and `err.response.body` at the catch site. No second request to learn what the server already told you, no stack trace that omits the 422 underneath. Issue #212 collected more thumbs-up than any other, sat open since 2023, and closed last week.

TypeScript types are generated from your OpenAPI spec at build time instead of typed by hand. Run `fetchkit codegen ./openapi.yaml`. A wrong spec gives you wrong types, which is at least honest.

## Breaking changes

`client.request()` returns a `Response` rather than parsed data. `client.json()` restores the old behavior. `transformResponse` is gone; write middleware. Node 18 is the floor.

Start with `npx fetchkit-migrate`. The codemod covered about 90% of our own call sites. The rest were people doing clever things with interceptors, and clever things need hands.

Docs are at fetchkit.dev/v2. The 1.x branch gets security patches for a year, then it stops.

# Fetchkit 2.0

Fetchkit 2.0 is out as of this morning.

One decision in version 1 was wrong from the start: every response got parsed as JSON before you saw it. Fine until somebody pushed a 200 MB CSV through and watched Node die. 2.0 hands you the raw stream and gets out of the way.

Three smaller things.

Retry config moved onto the request. Put `retry: { attempts: 4, on: [429, 503] }` on the one endpoint that keeps failing, rather than switching it on globally and hoping. Backoff honors `Retry-After`.

Errors carry the response now, and that is probably the change you notice first. At the catch site you read `err.response.status` and `err.response.body`. No follow-up request to find out what the server already said, no stack trace that hides the 422 underneath. Issue #212 drew more thumbs-up than anything else in the tracker, had been open since 2023, and closed last week.

TypeScript types come from your OpenAPI spec at build time instead of being written by hand. Run `fetchkit codegen ./openapi.yaml`. A wrong spec yields wrong types, which is at least honest.

## Breaking changes

`client.request()` returns a `Response`, not parsed data. `client.json()` gets the old behavior back. `transformResponse` is gone; write middleware. Node 18 is the minimum.

Begin with `npx fetchkit-migrate`. The codemod handled roughly 90% of our own call sites. What was left involved clever interceptor tricks, and clever needs hands.

Docs live at fetchkit.dev/v2. The 1.x branch gets security patches for a year, then nothing.
